headline: New law lets La Paz County, Arizona, buy about 3,400 acres of federal land at fair market value.
what_it_does: If La Paz County, Arizona, asks, the Interior Department must sell it about 3,400 acres of Bureau of Land Management land for fair market value. Land with significant cultural, environmental, wildlife, or recreational resources must be left out of the sale. The county must pay all costs of the transfer, and the land is closed to new mining claims, mineral or geothermal leases, and mineral material sales. The county and any later owners must take steps to protect tribal artifacts found on the land.

who_it_affects.how: The county can request and buy about 3,400 acres of federal land but must pay fair market value and all transfer costs.
Their Tribal Historic Preservation Office must be consulted to identify important artifacts, and tribal representatives may rebury any artifacts dug up near where they were found.
Anyone who later owns the land must make good faith efforts to avoid or limit disturbing tribal artifacts.
The land is no longer open to new mining claims, mineral or geothermal leases, or sales of mineral materials.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 29, 2025; the land transfer happens after La Paz County submits a request.
